    What is Picasso's most famous piece?
    Guernica
    “Guernica” is not only Picasso's best-known work, it's one of the most famous (and Google-searched) paintings in the world. Its depiction of an aerial bombing raid on the Basque town of Guernica in April 1937, during the Spanish Civil War, was an eerie visual prelude to the coming atrocities of World War II.Feb 3, 2020

    Did Pablo Picasso paint the Mona Lisa?
    Can't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.An AI Overview is not available for this search
    AI Overview
    No, Pablo Picasso did not paint the Mona Lisa. The Mona Lisa was painted by the Italian Renaissance artist Leonardo da Vinci. While Picasso was a suspect in the 1911 theft of the Mona Lisa from the Louvre Museum, he was eventually cleared of any involvement. The actual thief was Vincenzo Peruggia, an Italian patriot who wanted to return the painting to Italy.

      Did Van Gogh know Picasso?
      Pablo Picasso and Vincent Van Gogh never met. The Spanish painter discovered the Dutchman's work in Paris aged 19, when he was paying visits to independent salons. But an exercise in historical fiction leads one to surmise that had they met, they would not have gotten along.Feb 20, 2011

      Description

      Pablo Ruiz Picasso was a Spanish painter, sculptor, printmaker, ceramicist, and theatre designer who spent most of his adult life in France. Wikipedia
      Born: October 25, 1881, Málaga, Spain
      Died: April 8, 1973 (age 91 years), Mougins, France
      Periods: Cubism, Modern art, Surrealism, Picasso's Blue Period · See more
      Influenced by: Vincent van Gogh, Paul Cézanne · See more
      Full name: Pablo Diego José Francisco de Paula Juan Nepomuceno María de los Remedios Cipriano de la Santísima Trinidad Ruiz y Picasso
      Education: San Fernando Fine Art Royal Academy
